text:
April was blooming
before my window.
Among the jasmine
and the white roses
of a flower-filled balcony,
I saw the two sisters.
The younger sewed,
the elder spun …
Among the jasmine
and the white roses,
the littlest one,
laughing and rosy,
her needle in the air?,
looked toward my window.


The elder went on,
silent and pale,
the spindle on her distaff
coiling the linen.
April was blooming
before my window.


One clear afternoon
the elder was weeping,
among the jasmine
and the white roses,
and before the white linen
she spun on her distaff.
What is wrong? I said to her.
Silent, pale,
she pointed to the dress
the sister had begun.
On the black tunic
the needle gleamed;
over the white veil,
the silver thimble.
She pointed to the April
afternoon that dreamed,
while the ringing of bells
could be heard.
And in the clear afternoon
she showed me her tears…
April was blooming
before my window.


It was another joyful April
and another peaceful afternoon.
The flower-filled balcony
was solitary…
Neither the littlest one,
laughing and rosy,
nor the sad sister,
silent and pale,
nor the black tunic,
nor the white coif…
Only on the spindle
the linen turned
by an invisible hand,
and in the dark room
the moon in the clean
mirror shone…
Among the jasmine
and the white roses
of the flower-filled balcony,
I looked at myself in the clear
moon of the mirror
that dreamed far away…
April was blooming
before my window.

translation.title: April Was Blooming
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish rendering. The source body lacks the opening phrase supplied by the catalog title and begins with ‘frente a mi ventana’; ‘April was blooming’ has been restored as the first line, matching the later refrain, and this restoration is explicit here. Source stanza breaks and ellipses are retained.
